_note: Every data source the project uses or has considered, with the partition it belongs to and the roles it may serve.

Three partitions, never blended. real_india is the target domain and the only partition that can make the `domain` claim true. real_external is real footage outside the target country or traffic regime: an external-domain test, and training data only under a declared protocol. synthetic_sumo is simulator output: it may pretrain count-based models and may never appear in any evaluation split.

Roles are separate gates because one source can pass one and fail another. BMD-45 is the right detector data and cannot feed the forecaster, because 45,986 stills over 3,679 cameras is about 12.5 frames per camera and a window needs 120 continuous seconds from one.

scripts/check_sources.py enforces the gate. A source marked accepted for a role that it does not pass fails the check; a source in_use reports what it still owes; a rejected source must say why. Licence is recorded as found, and `resolved` means someone has established that derived data may be redistributed, not that the footage is publicly viewable.
Cameras already in the corpus are not duplicated here: the youtube_corpus entry points at data/cameras.json, and each camera's partition is derived from its declared country and traffic type.

youtube_corpus.name: Third-party YouTube uploads used to build the forecasting corpus
youtube_corpus.reason: Built before the gate existed. Every camera still owes a licence, and none of the four fold-eligible cameras is Indian.

bmd45.name: BMD-45, Bengaluru Safe City CCTV (arXiv 2604.24419)
bmd45.reason: Stills, about 12.5 frames per camera; no camera holds the 120 continuous seconds one window needs. Confirmed from the metadata 2026-10-15: no camera id, no per-image time, ids spread over ~1M with the longest consecutive run 4; the README says frames were sampled for temporal diversity from long-duration Bengaluru Police Safe City recordings (February 2025), which are the route to sequences.

idd.name: India Driving Dataset, IIIT Hyderabad
idd.licence: research use via registered account; cite the IDD paper
idd.reason: Dashcam, not a fixed elevated camera. Research-use terms do not establish redistribution of derived data.

chennai_zenodo_21545806.name: Chennai Traffic Dataset, Zenodo record 21545806 (2026-07-25)
chennai_zenodo_21545806.reason: Inspected 2026-10-15 by reading the archive directory over HTTP ranges and viewing one frame. 1,855 images in two sequences, source frame indices 0-2744 and 0-1890 sampled at every second frame or coarser. Even at 25 fps the longer sequence is about 110 s, below the 120 s one window spans. The frame viewed is road-level from a moving vehicle, not a fixed elevated camera. Plates are already blurred.

campus_recording.name: Part B campus capture, six-viewpoint evaluation set (S19)
campus_recording.licence: own footage, subject to institutional permission
campus_recording.reason: Blocked on the faculty guide since 2026-08-22. The only route identified so far that can be licence-clean, Indian, fixed, elevated and continuous at once.

sumo_synthetic.name: SUMO count sequences at the project intersection (ADR-024)
sumo_synthetic.reason: Counts and queues only, no pixels. May pretrain count baselines and the linear probe; may never enter an evaluation split or be counted toward any claim.

bellevue.name: Bellevue Traffic Video Dataset, City of Bellevue, WA (github.com/City-of-Bellevue/TrafficVideoDataset)
bellevue.licence: none stated; README says 'made available for research purposes', repository licence field is null
bellevue.reason: Assessed 2026-10-15 from the README and the official sample frame of three of the five cameras. About 101 h of 1280x720 30 Hz video from September 2017, five pole-mounted intersection cameras, hosted as Google Drive folders. Each view frames a whole junction - every approach in one shot - which matches the deployment geometry better than any camera in the corpus, and a burnt-in timestamp makes continuity checkable. Against it: strong wide-angle distortion, a dome housing occluding the bottom of the frame, and lane-disciplined US traffic with no two- or three-wheelers, so it is the M6 regime, not the target one. Owes: a licence that permits the intended use, continuous duration per file, and HIGH support once labelled.
